market.title: AI vs. the rest of the economy
Scoop: AI companies plot "day after" scenarios for public revolt
market.summary: Top executives at Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI companies are privately gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt after a catastrophic AI event . Why it matters : These officials anticipate a large-scale event, most likely a cyberattack, that shuts down access to financial services, internet connectivity, or even power and water. The first example of significant real-world harm caused by unsafe AI would turn an already wary public further against the technology and its leaders, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, as well as President Trump for reluctance to regulate it. The risk : While scenario planning is common within many companies and national security settings — the Pentagon has been running war games for decades — the difference is that many top AI researchers and executives believe a major incident is inevitable . "OpenAI conducts preparedness exercises where teams discuss and work through a range of potential scenarios," a company spokesperson said. "These scenarios are not treated as inevitable, but are meant to help us prepare for a variety of circumstances." Anthropic declined to comment. Zoom in: The blame game will start whether a rogue-agent swarm breaks containment from an internal testing environment or a bad actor finds unexpected ways to use available models. A recent campaign targeting South Korean financial organizations — including reported breaches at two banks — shows the damage one person can do. A hacker from China allegedly used AI tools from China-developed models, including DeepSeek, to steal data from tens of thousands of bank customers. The attacker used Claude Code to ask for help finding places to sell the stolen data, according to cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike . Top AI planners assume Democrats , ascendant after the midterms, will move fast to shut down AI but will face significant challenges. An aging Congress, out of touch with the AI revolution, could find itself out of its depth. The global economy is now heavily intertwined with an AI infrastructure buildout. Slowing it down could hit an already fragile economy hard. Too many open-weight models exist that can already be freely downloaded and used to cause harm, a problem most cybersecurity pros see as solvable only by using AI to fight rogue AI . Between the lines : The planning involves red-teaming for worst-case scenarios. It focuses mainly on racing to educate members of Congress. Company executives know regulation has no chance of passing right now, but still want to shape the legislation and policies U.S. leaders will turn to after a first catastrophic event. What we're watching: Many AI industry insiders told Axios they believe a major event will occur in the next six to 12 months. Even with Democrats in control of the House and Senate, the companies see fractured politics as the norm, including within the Democratic Party. Some of the most heavy-handed Democratic proposals include banning superintelligence or pausing advanced AI development. Others have bipartisan support and even some industry buy-in, including a required kill switch on advanced AI. But experts have questioned the viability of trying to turn off all AI systems. The bottom line: In a real crisis, Washington can set partisan differences aside. One Democratic aide pointed to cooperation during COVID and the 2008 financial crisis.

headlines.title: HALO Wins Court Order Blocking Merck's Keytruda SC in Europe

The ruling does not affect Keytruda's intravenous version. This marks another legal victory for Halozyme against Merck, though the company clarified that its separate ENHANZE technology and licensing business remain unaffected.

headlines.title: Bayer Seeks Kerendia Label Expansion in Non-Diabetic CKD

The approval is based on positive phase III FIND-CKD trial data showing the drug significantly delayed kidney disease progression and reduced cardiovascular-kidney events. This expansion broadens Kerendia's addressable market and strengthens Bayer's cardiovascular and renal portfolio, with the drug already approved for diabetic CKD and heart failure in multiple markets.

headlines.title: NVS Wins FDA Nod for Label Expansion of Immunology Drug Rhapsido
headlines.summary: Novartis received FDA approval for Rhapsido (remibrutinib) for symptomatic dermographism (SD), making it the only prescription treatment approved for both CSU and SD, the two most common forms of chronic hives. The approval was supported by phase III RemIND trial data showing 29.3% complete hive resolution at week 12 versus 14% for placebo. The company is also evaluating remibrutinib in multiple sclerosis, hidradenitis suppurativa, and food allergy. However, Novartis faces pipeline setbacks with failed trials for pelacarsen and del-desiran, and generic competition pressuring blockbuster drugs.

headlines.title: AbbVie's Temab-A Gets Two FDA Breakthrough Therapy Tags in Cancer
headlines.summary: AbbVie announced that its investigational antibody-drug conjugate Temab-A (telisotuzumab adizutecan) has received two FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations for colorectal cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. The designations were based on data from the M21-404 study, and the company is evaluating Temab-A across multiple advanced solid tumors as part of its expanding oncology pipeline.

BMY.title: Pfizer's Oncology Outlook: Key Drivers to Watch Ahead of Q3 Results
BMY.summary: Pfizer's oncology revenues rose 3% to $4.17 billion in Q2 2026, representing 27% of total revenues. The company expects Q3 growth driven by newer drugs like Padcev, Lorbrena, and Braftovi-Mektovi, offset by declines in Ibrance and Adcetris. Pfizer is advancing the dual PD-1/VEGF inhibitor PF-08634404 across nine studies including two pivotal phase III trials. The stock trades at an attractive valuation with a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

BMY.title: AbbVie's Temab-A Gets Two FDA Breakthrough Therapy Tags in Cancer
BMY.summary: AbbVie announced that its investigational antibody-drug conjugate Temab-A (telisotuzumab adizutecan) has received two FDA Breakthrough Therapy designations for colorectal cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. The designations were based on data from the M21-404 study, and the company is evaluating Temab-A across multiple advanced solid tumors as part of its expanding oncology pipeline.

BMY.summary: Aardvark Therapeutics appointed David Zhang, Ph.D., MBA, as an independent board director, bringing over 25 years of clinical development and regulatory expertise from companies including MyoKardia, Genentech/Roche, Alumis, and Abivax. IONS.title: NVS Wins FDA Nod for Label Expansion of Immunology Drug Rhapsido
IONS.summary: Novartis received FDA approval for Rhapsido (remibrutinib) for symptomatic dermographism (SD), making it the only prescription treatment approved for both CSU and SD, the two most common forms of chronic hives. The approval was supported by phase III RemIND trial data showing 29.3% complete hive resolution at week 12 versus 14% for placebo. The company is also evaluating remibrutinib in multiple sclerosis, hidradenitis suppurativa, and food allergy. However, Novartis faces pipeline setbacks with failed trials for pelacarsen and del-desiran, and generic competition pressuring blockbuster drugs.

PGY.title: Will PGY's Expanding Funding Base Reduce Its Reliance on ABS Markets?
PGY.summary: Pagaya Technologies raised $3.7 billion across six asset-backed securities (ABS) transactions in Q2 2026 and added 11 new institutional investors, bringing the total to 174. The company is diversifying its funding model beyond traditional securitization through auto funding facilities, variable funding notes, and revolving personal-loan facilities. Despite expanding alternative funding sources, Pagaya completed a $600 million personal-loan securitization, bringing 2026 ABS issuance to over $9 billion, demonstrating that securitization remains a core funding engine.

BULL.title: Can Webull's Regulatory Troubles Give Robinhood a Competitive Edge?
BULL.summary: Robinhood is positioned to attract Webull customers as the rival faces heightened regulatory scrutiny over alleged China-related ties from a bipartisan U.S. House committee. Robinhood is leveraging transfer incentives, emphasizing its American roots and data security focus to appeal to active traders. The company's expanding product portfolio and user-friendly platform strengthen its competitive position, though actual customer migration remains unconfirmed.

BULL.title: Will State Regulators Slow Robinhood's Prediction-Market Growth?
BULL.summary: Robinhood Markets faces regulatory headwinds in its rapidly growing prediction-market business as U.S. states, led by Ohio, attempt to classify sports-event contracts as gambling rather than federally regulated derivatives. Despite event-contract revenues surging to $156 million in Q2 2026, the Ohio Casino Control Commission's cease-and-desist order and similar actions across other states could fragment the market and limit growth potential for Robinhood and competitors.
